problem: The permanent trusted gate must not require a second human GitHub account. Because the currently trusted base policy itself enforces that rule, the change requires a one-time two-phase migration using the already-existing bootstrap workflow, followed immediately by bootstrap removal under the new autonomous trusted policy.

decision.rationale: Preserve the base-authoritative trust boundary without making BeBee depend on a second reviewer. Phase 1 changes the trusted policy while temporarily retaining the pre-existing bootstrap workflow; phase 2 removes the bootstrap once the autonomous trusted policy is authoritative in main.

official_docs.verified_constraint: Required status checks should use unique job names; duplicate names are acceptable only as a documented temporary migration state and must be removed immediately after the policy transition.

alternatives.reason: Conflicts with the owner's intended solo-agent workflow and creates an operational dependency unrelated to evidence quality.
Would require a manual repository-settings exception and temporarily weaken main protection.
Uses the already-existing bootstrap route once, keeps repository protection enabled, then removes the bootstrap under the new trusted policy.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The trusted policy no longer requires an independent second-human GitHub approval for governance or P2/P4/P6 progress.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: check_trust_boundary.py, pr-evidence-trusted.yml, DECISIONS.md and the PR template remove the mandatory reviewer dependency.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The permanent workflow remains base-authoritative and never executes candidate policy code as authority.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: pr-evidence-trusted.yml retains separate trusted/candidate checkouts and executes validators from trusted/.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The existing bootstrap workflow is explicitly temporary and a follow-up PR removes it immediately after this policy transition lands.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/16-ci-trust-boundary.md defines bootstrap cleanup as the next migration phase; this PR intentionally retains the bootstrap only to cross the old-policy boundary.

automated: Both the existing bootstrap validation and the base-authoritative trusted validation are observed on this migration PR; the trusted failure is expected to be only the old second-human rule until main adopts the new policy.
manual: Direct write to protected main was previously rejected by the repository ruleset, confirming that the migration must remain PR-based.

governance.trust_boundary_change: Removes the mandatory second-human dependency while preserving base-authoritative policy execution. The existing bootstrap workflow remains only for this transition and is removed in the immediately following PR.
governance.bypass_analysis: Candidate policy still cannot become the trusted authority within the same PR. Reference diversity, diff classification, official-doc parsing, same-PR governance evidence and previous-base adversarial tests remain enforced. The temporary duplicate required context is explicitly bounded to this migration only.
governance.rollback: Revert this PR to restore the previous mandatory-review rule. If phase 1 lands, phase 2 may simply delete the bootstrap workflow without changing the autonomous trusted policy.

known_limitations: Until the immediate phase-2 cleanup PR merges, both bootstrap and trusted workflows coexist temporarily.
Repository ruleset strict/up-to-date enforcement remains a separate GitHub settings action tracked in issue #4.
